column1: # targets: items separated by |. Each item is a glob, or file::regex (a grep test), or - for none.
#   What a target IS depends on kind: stage — an artefact the stage leaves; gate — the ruling record; check — an input the
#   guard reads (intake.md), never an artefact. A reader attributing files to stages skips check rows.
#   A glob prefixed ? is CLAIMED but not REQUIRED: it stops the unmapped sweep naming the file, and does not make the stage done.
#   On a gate row, a file::regex target is the ruling record: when it matches, the gate is RULED rather than inferred.
# exclude: regex applied to matched paths, or -.  skipif: file::pattern — when it matches, the stage counts as skipped by design.
# critic: path pattern for the reviewer pass, with {id} (the row id) or {file} (a critic file whose first lines name the artefact);
#   several patterns separated by |, tried in order; n/a for a stage no critic reviews (a proxy pass); - when the command does not say.
# since: the plugin version the row entered the method. A stage missing while later stages are done is reported once, with this.
# waits: what this row cannot start before, outside its own arc — ARC:ID. Inside an arc the order is the dependency.
# storyline: the storyline stage this row begins (strategy, portfolio, prioritisation, choice, specification). Blank = the row sits
#   inside the stage of the row before it; - = belongs to no storyline stage. Read by storyline-review, not by the renderer.
# ⛔ A stage that adds an artefact adds a row here AND a line to the command's resume map AND a directory to its scan. Same edit.
